property_summary: The return value of transfer() must be true when it completes successfully; the mutant returns false, violating this invariant.
For any call to transfer that does not revert, the returned boolean must match the success of the internal calls; the mutant always returns false regardless of success.

The reference function never reverts when called with a non-empty tos array; the buggy function always reverts due to require(false), so the property "transfer does not revert" holds for all admissible inputs on the reference but fails on the mutant.

For any non-empty address array _tos, the reference transfer call succeeds and returns true, while the buggy version always reverts; a fuzzer-chosen adversarial callee that reverts on transferFrom is deployed so the revert flag distinguishes the two.

For any non-empty _tos array and any caddress that is a contract, the reference returns true while the buggy version always reverts because require(false) fires before the external call, so catching the revert distinguishes them.

For any non-empty address array _tos and any caddress, the reference contract always returns true (and the call does not revert) because it attempts the loop; the buggy version always reverts due to the require(false), so the return value is never true.
For any non-empty _tos array the function completes and returns true; the buggy version silently succeeds on empty _tos as well, violating the original requirement that empty _tos must revert.
For any input, a non-empty _tos array guarantees the call does not revert; the mutant succeeds on empty _tos while the original reverts.
For any call to transfer(...), the call reverts if and only if the _tos array is empty; the mutant violates this by not reverting on empty _tos.
Any call to transfer that provides an empty _tos array must revert; the mutant incorrectly succeeds without reverting.
For any call to transfer, the transaction must revert if the _tos array is empty; the buggy version does not revert on empty _tos.
The correct contract never reverts due to out-of-bounds access, while the buggy version reverts for any input where the callee contract does not revert on the extra call with zero address.

The reference correctly returns true after a successful zero-length loop (or all external calls succeed), while the buggy version silently returns false for the same inputs, violating the invariant that a valid non-reverting transfer with _tos.length>0 should return true.
